message:
Run the declared models where a model suite leaves selectors implicit

The relationship and queue factories and the misinformation check in
WorldView read policy_registry keys directly, so a suite without
per-domain selectors (Scenario editor presets, prepare without a
registry) ran legacy defaults while manifests and Checkpoints recorded
the suite's models (#169). They now resolve through selected_models.

Such a suite is signed model_suite@2, so a Checkpoint captured before is
refused instead of switching models mid-Run; a suite with every selector
explicit keeps @1. The behavior policy comparison now compares declared
models only and refuses a Run recorded at @1 with implicit selectors.

message:
Count a high-distress recovery that happens during event handling

The distress monitor closed a run only when the psychology update itself
crossed the threshold. Staff support can lower distress while events
are handled, so the next update saw both values low, left the run open
and later overwrote it without counting the recovery (#159). A run now
closes whenever either value is below the threshold, and a rise in the
same update starts a new episode.

message:
Count people walking to a zone when admitting a return or an arrival

Travel admission holds a place in the destination zone from departure:
it refuses to start when occupancy plus everyone already walking there
reaches the capacity. A return or relocation counted only return
travel, and an arrival counted nobody walking, so either could take the
walker's place and the walker's arrival overfilled the zone, stopping
the run at the per-tick invariant (#180).

incoming_travelers in domain/temporary_spaces now counts everyone moving
to the zone or one of its facilities, and travel, return, relocation and
arrival admission all use it. A return or arrival without a place waits
and is admitted when one opens.

message:
Take a facility out of service on time and let its current user finish

An operator-entered facility outage, equipment failure or power outage
failed when the facility was in use at its start, because the units
left would fall below active occupancy. It never took effect, and its
recovery failed too (#188). Generated Scenarios have one unit per

served finishes, and service never starts beyond the working units, so

Evaluate guards on floor plan changes against their target

Guards find the facility or zone they compare in the event payload's
facility_id, staff_id, zone_id or resource_id. Floor plan changes keep

zone.occupancy guard on set_partition failed with "no facility target"
or "no known zone target", whether it held or not, and the approved
change never ran (#194). Only floor plan payloads carry a top-level

message:
Refuse plan mistakes with a reason the Project screen can show

Plan previews let ValueError through, which the server answers with a bare
"invalid project request" 400, so an operator tracing a plan never learned
why it was refused (#204). Some type and reference mistakes did not even
raise ValueError: they failed with StopIteration or TypeError, an HTTP 500
(#202).

PlanServices.preview now runs each operation in _operation_result and
turns its ValueError into a StorageError coded plan_<operation>_invalid,
which the server returns as a 409 with the message. Contract errors name
the field and the rule but not the value. A Scenario preview with a
selected plan does the same as scenario_plan_invalid, and a plan upload
that is not JSON is invalid_plan_json.

The seven crashes are now reasoned ValueErrors: an equipment footprint of
a facility in an unknown zone, and GeoJSON numbers, LineString coordinates
and envelope lists of the wrong type.

message:
Keep the regional research going when a public service drops the connection

urllib wraps only connection errors in URLError. A connection closed
before the response (RemoteDisconnected), reset while reading, or a body
cut short (IncompleteRead) reached the research raw, so one flaky public
service failed the whole Scenario preview with HTTP 500 (#208). e-Stat
JSON that was not an object failed with AttributeError the same way.

The JSON fetches now turn every OSError and http.client.HTTPException
into RegionProviderError, as the shelter CSV download already did, and
the e-Stat client requires a JSON object. The research then reports the
service as unknown and keeps the others.

An e-Stat table that counts everyone in a 総数 class of its age axis was
dropped as a whole, and the Scenario silently fell back to assumed ages
(#209). Most population tables have that class. Five-year bands beside a
subtotal such as 15歳未満 passed the reader instead and failed the whole
preview in the population generator.

Rows labelled exactly 総数, 総計, 合計 or 計 are now left out of the age
and household-size axes. Overlapping age ranges leave the statistics
unused like repeated ones. population_statistics_notes tells the operator,
in the Scenario warnings, which total rows were left out or that the
statistics could not be used and assumptions were.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
Test the storage paths an operator reaches from the CLI and the Project screen

The project CLI (sheltersim project) had no test that ran it, and the Run
measurements, the history index rebuild and the recovery of interrupted
Runs were reachable from the Project screen but untested.

Run the CLI from create through prepare, approval, compute, fork, frame,
history, usage, rerun, archive and delete, with the regional research
answered by the fake public services. Check that measured computations
and render reports are kept beside the Run and malformed reports are
refused, that each Branch's index is ready and a rebuild keeps every
history, and that a Run left running or queued is interrupted at restart
and then resumes to the same world as an uninterrupted one.

One bug found is a strict xfail: a rebuild drops the action decisions
recorded while the Run computed (#213).

message:
Refuse to rebuild a history index that matches its Branch

The action and dialogue decisions recorded while a Run computes are
written only to its history index, never to a Checkpoint. Rebuilding the
index from Checkpoints therefore dropped them for good, and the Project
screen offered the rebuild even for a current index (#213).

HistoryIndex.rebuild now refuses with history_index_current when the
index head matches the Branch head, so it serves only Runs without an
index or with a stale one. Its limits say the recorded decisions are not
restored.

message:
Keep only rules and procedures in the testing guide

docs/testing.md had grown to 491 lines as every change rewrote its
per-file test map, its owner totals, a one-line history of every count,
dated coverage and timing figures, and the record of analyses long since
acted on. Tests keep changing, so those figures were always about to be
stale.

Keep how to run, read and measure the tests, where tests go and what
they share, how to test interventions, and what to do on finding a bug.
Drop the test map and its totals, the coverage table and its per-area
notes, the migration record and the analysis of gaps; their history is
in git and the Issues. Count tests with pytest --collect-only instead.

Test files may now import the stateless synthetic data of tests/support/
as they already import fixture paths; anything with state or cleanup
stays a fixture.

message:
Batch history index writes and measure storage usage with scandir

Saving a Checkpoint spent much of its time indexing the new records and
rescanning the store for its size (#47). Each indexed record ran its own
SELECT, INSERTs and generation upsert, privacy-checked every integer
through a JSON encoder, matched every field name against the private
field pattern and hashed its payload twice. The index connection kept
SQLite's 2 MiB page cache, so a growing index spilled pages within the
transaction, syncing the journal before each spill. usage() listed the
store with rglob and made several stat calls per file.

Index records now go through a batch that inserts the rows of up to 500
records at a time, in the order they were put, and adds the generation
counts per kind. A key put earlier in the batch or already stored still
must carry the same payload, and a refused or over-capacity write still
rolls back. The write connection holds a 16 MiB page cache; the journal
mode and synchronous setting are unchanged, so the commit syncs as
before. safe_document passes built-in ints as it passes finite floats
and caches the private field-name match. usage() walks the store with
os.scandir, one stat per regular file, still measuring the disk at each
call so other processes' files count; a file removed while measured
counts as no bytes.

For 100 people over 360 and 1440 minutes on the ProjectAPI route, every
table of the index and the world, events and metrics hashes equal those
before the change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
Share the parsed facility geometry and spatial constraints within a phase

Tick phases parse the facility geometry once per raw config through
geometry_config_scope, but several callers still parsed it themselves,
and movement parsed the spatial constraints again at every call (#45).
Its _spatial_constraints returned the effective constraints as a JSON
dump, and route_is_physically_clear, plan_in_room_route, queue slots and
facility approaches each validated that dump into a new model.

_spatial_constraints now returns the effective SpatialConstraints model
itself. It is built from validated walls, obstacles and footprints and
SpatialConstraints has no model-wide validator, so the dump parsed again
was an equal model. The new parsed_facility_geometry returns the
Scenario's geometry without runtime overrides and, inside a config
scope, shares the parse effective_geometry uses. Facility queues, the
operational demand snapshot, runner routes, population arrivals and the
arrival effect check use it; outside a scope it parses at each call as
before.

For 100 people the world, events and metrics hashes equal those before
the change over 360 and 1440 minutes of the generated Scenario and 360
minutes of the 100-person fixture Scenario.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
Reuse saved history conversions between Checkpoint saves of one advance

Each save of an advance converted the whole WorldState and KPI history to
JSON, hashed it twice, deep-copied and restored all of it for the restore
check, and encoded it again for the archive, so a save got slower the
longer the Run was (#44). Most of that is append-only history.

TimelineStore's advance loop now passes a CheckpointHistoryCache to each
capture. For the EventLog, KPI and resource samples and the append-only
model_state histories (body-state window, shared operations, resource
audit, request and stall histories) it keeps each item's document and
canonical bytes, and for EventLog records the record the previous restore
check built. Items are matched by identity; histories that drop their
oldest entries are handled, and plain-dict entries are reused only while
they still equal their document. A CanonicalEncoder splices the cached
bytes into the state and checkpoint hashes and the archive chunks, and
the restore check parses only new EventLog records and shares the cached
lists instead of copying them. Both full validations stay as before.

Checkpoint v1 bytes, hashes, manifests and chunks are unchanged: over
1440 minutes of the generated Scenario all 49 manifests and 3332 chunks
equal those of develop, as do the world, event and metric hashes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
